note: The closest sibling is concurrent-writers: both live in a repo with other writers, but scoped-commit is the mechanics of getting exactly my files into one commit right now, while concurrent-writers is the coordination protocol for vanished commits, leases and history rewrites. Other negatives are near-misses on repo-extract (a whole folder becoming its own repo), ci-cd-pipelines (what happens after a commit lands), handoff (the write-up rather than the commit) and automated-code-review (a check that blocks bad commits).

queries.query: git status is showing forty-odd modified files across four different projects and maybe six of them are mine from this afternoon. i want a commit with exactly those in it and nothing else - i usually just stage everything and regret it later

one file has my new parser function in it and also a load of half finished stuff from yesterday that definitely isn't ready to go anywhere. can i get just my part of that file in without dragging the rest along

the trailer at the bottom of all our commits names a model version that hasn't run on this machine since spring, so every commit is crediting something that didn't do the work. what should that line actually say going forward

last time i committed, a stray build folder went in with it and i only noticed about a week later. before i pull the trigger this time i want to actually see that what's staged is exactly what i think it is
i've finished the parse change - three files under src/parse plus one test file. get that in with a decent message explaining why, and leave the remote completely alone, nobody pushes from this box

a commit i made monday is just gone from main after someone rebased, and last week my staged work ended up inside a different session's commit entirely. how do several of us work this repo without eating each other's changes
queries.why: Near-miss on concurrent-writers: lost history and coordination between writers, not staging one clean commit.

queries.query: the wrapper folder in my workspace has become a real project of its own and i want it living on github by itself, without dragging the renders or anything sensitive along with it
queries.why: Near-miss on repo-extract: carving a folder into its own repo, which is the one place a full staging sweep is correct.

queries.query: i want pushes to main to build the thing once, tag the artifact, and then promote that same artifact through staging rather than rebuilding it at every stage
queries.why: Near-miss on ci-cd-pipelines: what happens after a commit lands, not how the commit is assembled.

queries.query: i'm done for the day - write up what changed, what i actually verified versus assumed, and what's still open for the next person, and keep the durable bits somewhere they'll resurface
queries.why: Near-miss on handoff: the completion record, which sits alongside the commit but is a different artifact.

queries.query: i want something that automatically stops anyone committing a key or a token into this repo, ideally before it ever reaches a branch anyone else can see
queries.why: Near-miss on automated-code-review: a machine-enforced rule in the review pipeline, not the discipline of one deliberate commit.
